title: This time it’s Iowa’s late field goal that secures victory in Cy-Hawk rivalry
content:
IOWA CITY, Iowa — The contest didn’t quite go as expected, but Iowa will not quibble with the result against its in-state rival.

A 14-point favorite, No. 21 Iowa survived the annual Cy-Hawk game on kicker Caden Buhr’s 42-yard field goal with 15 seconds remaining to beat Iowa State 16-13 on Saturday night at Kinnick Stadium. The Hawkeyes trailed Iowa State 10-0 in the second quarter before tying the score at halftime and later in the fourth quarter.

Buhr, a second-year non-scholarship player from Bettendorf, Iowa, drilled three field goals for the Hawkeyes (2-0). The victory ended Iowa’s two-game losing streak to the Cyclones, who had won the two previous matchups on dramatic field goals of their own. Iowa now has control of all four of its traveling trophies, which includes rivalry games against Iowa State, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Nebraska.

There was a bit of fear on the Iowa side after the Cyclones connected on a last-second pass to midfield in which the clock seemingly ran out. Officials put one second on the clock, and the Cyclones offense lined up on the ball. But unlike last week’s controversial result in the Michigan-Western Michigan matchup, the game concluded because Iowa State did not have a timeout remaining and the clock automatically started when the ball was marked for play.

Iowa started quarterback Hank Brown, who played the entire game after seemingly winning a competition with Jeremy Hecklinski. Brown completed 21 of 30 passes for 191 yards and rushed for the Hawkeyes’ only touchdown.

Buhr’s heroics ended counterpart Kyle Konrardy’s attempt toward knocking out the Hawkeyes for the third straight season with a late field goal. Two years ago, Konrardy’s 54-yard field goal came with 6 seconds left to win 20-19 at Kinnick. Last year in Ames, Konrardy hit another 54-yarder, this time with 1:52 left, in a 13-10 victory.

Iowa State quarterback Jaylen Raynor completed 10 of 19 passes for 117 yards and one touchdown. The Cyclones surprisingly outrushed Iowa 138-93.
